title: Animation Retiming with Motion Warping Curves
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive animation retiming system with motion warping curves. The scene must include:

## Scene Setup
- Dark background (0x1a1a2e) with a ground plane (20x20, color 0x2a2a3a) at y=0.
- A perspective camera at (0, 3, 8) looking at origin.
- Ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) from (5, 10, 5).
- OrbitControls for camera manipulation.
- Three animated objects on the ground plane:
  1. A red sphere (radius 0.4) labeled 'A' that follows a circular path (radius 3, center at origin, in the xz-plane).
  2. A green box (0.6x0.6x0.6) labeled 'B' that follows a figure-8 (lemniscate) path (scale 3, in xz-plane).
  3. A blue cone (radius 0.3, height 0.8) labeled 'C' that follows a linear back-and-forth path along x from -4 to 4.
- Each object also bobs vertically (sine wave, amplitude 0.3) as a secondary motion channel.

## Warping Curve System
- Implement a time warping system where each object has its own warp curve that maps normalized global time [0,1] to warped local time [0,1].
- Support 4 warp curve presets:
  - 'linear': identity mapping t_out = t_in
  - 'easeInOut': cubic ease-in-out (smooth start and end)
  - 'easeIn': quadratic ease-in (slow start, fast end)
  - 'easeOut': quadratic ease-out (fast start, slow end)
- The warp curve is applied per-object, so each object can have a different curve.
- The warped time must be monotonically non-decreasing (enforce this).

## Global Timeline
- A global animation timeline that loops from 0.0 to 1.0 over a configurable duration (default 4 seconds).
- The timeline can be played, paused, and scrubbed.
- A global speed multiplier (default 1.0) that scales the rate of timeline progression.

## HUD / UI (DOM overlay)
- A top bar showing: current global time (0.000-1.000, 3 decimal places), play/pause state, speed multiplier.
- For each object (A, B, C), show: name, current warp curve preset name, warped local time (3 decimals).
- Buttons:
  - 'Play/Pause' button (id='btn-play-pause') toggles playback.
  - 'Reset' button (id='btn-reset') resets global time to 0 and sets all curves to 'linear'.
  - Per-object curve cycle buttons (ids: 'btn-curve-a', 'btn-curve-b', 'btn-curve-c') that cycle through the 4 presets in order: linear -> easeInOut -> easeIn -> easeOut -> linear...
  - 'Speed Up' (id='btn-speed-up') increases speed multiplier by 0.25 (max 3.0).
  - 'Speed Down' (id='btn-speed-down') decreases speed multiplier by 0.25 (min 0.25).
  - 'Undo' button (id='btn-undo') that undoes the last curve change (maintain a history stack of up to 20 entries).
  - 'Redo' button (id='btn-redo') that redoes a previously undone curve change.

## Keyboard Controls
- Space: toggle play/pause
- R: reset
- 1/2/3: cycle warp curve for object A/B/C respectively
- Up arrow: speed up
- Down arrow: speed down
- Ctrl+Z: undo
- Ctrl+Y: redo
- S: scrub mode toggle. When scrub mode is on, left/right arrow keys move global time by 0.01 increments.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- globalTime: number (0.0 to 1.0, current normalized global time)
- isPlaying: boolean
- speedMultiplier: number
- scrubMode: boolean
- objects: { a: { warpCurve: string, warpedTime: number, position: {x,y,z} }, b: {...}, c: {...} }
- undoStackSize: number (current undo history length)
- redoStackSize: number (current redo history length)
- totalFrames: number (frame counter since page load)
- warpMonotonic: boolean (true if all warped times are monotonically valid this frame)
- curveOrder: [string, string, string] (current curve names for A, B, C in order)

## Important Constraints
- All warped times must remain in [0,1] and be monotonically non-decreasing as global time increases.
- Object positions must be NaN-free at all times.
- The undo/redo system must correctly restore per-object curve assignments.
- When paused, objects must freeze at their current warped positions.
- Speed multiplier changes must not cause time jumps (smooth continuation).
- The global time must wrap cleanly from 1.0 back to 0.0 without discontinuities in object positions.
physics_constraints: Warped time must be monotonically non-decreasing within each cycle. All object positions must be NaN-free. Global time must stay in [0,1]. Speed multiplier bounded [0.25, 3.0]. Undo/redo stack integrity must be maintained (undo reverses last curve change exactly, redo re-applies it).
